answer: An operator that abandons 31 aliases after a single epoch thus destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the ember forfeiture shows up in the voyage totals with the opal audit listing each retired key. Retiring an identity early forfeits 18% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
